key_insight: Mesoscale neural operators learn nonlocal constitutive laws from molecular dynamics while preserving strain energy density and fracture energy across horizon rescaling.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables continuum fracture simulations on domains far larger than atomistic training specimens while retaining learned nanoscale material behavior.
method: Learn a nonlocal kernel and nonlinear constitutive relation from MD loading and displacement data.
Normalize the kernel to preserve strain energy density under horizon rescaling.
Rescale critical bond stretch to maintain a consistent energy release rate across scales.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests recovered the underlying nonlocal model; MD-based tests matched energy metrics within 3% and out-of-distribution peak forces within 6%, with fracture branching demonstrated on a plate 4,000 times the training-specimen area.
watch_item: The reported tests do not establish generalization to other materials or loading regimes; cross-scale consistency alone does not guarantee predictive accuracy.
paper_title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
